from PIL import Image
import numpy as np, colorsys
im = np.asarray(Image.open('barcode.png')).astype(float)
stripe = im.mean(axis=0)/255.0
lum = 0.2126*stripe[:,0]+0.7152*stripe[:,1]+0.0722*stripe[:,2]
# saturation & hue per stripe (hsv)
mx = stripe.max(axis=1); mn = stripe.min(axis=1)
sat = np.where(mx>0,(mx-mn)/np.maximum(mx,1e-9),0)
print('mean sat', sat.mean(), 'mean lum', lum.mean())
# brightness percentiles
for p in [5,25,50,75,95,99,100]:
    print('p%d'%p, round(np.percentile(lum,p),1))
# R-B bias overall
print('mean R,G,B:', (stripe.mean(axis=0)*255).round(1))
# list the 15 brightest stripes
idx = np.argsort(lum)[::-1][:15]
print('brightest stripes:', sorted(idx.tolist()))
# top 15 most saturated
idx2 = np.argsort(sat)[::-1][:15]
print('most saturated:', sorted(idx2.tolist()))
"

## Summary of the analysis

**Target barcode profile** (1000 stripes): extremely dark film — mean stripe luminance 40/255, median ~25/255, **no stripe brighter than 148**, 59% of stripes below 40, 81% below 60; nearly neutral palette with a slight blue cast (RGB 39/40/41), dim warm-brown patches, and one unmistakable pale slate-blue block at 9–10.5% of runtime with color ≈ RGB(129,151,181).

**Comparing against all candidates** using only auto-generated thumbnail/preview frames (no videos streamed or downloaded):

| Candidate | mean L | max L | <60 share | corr with target |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Nosferatu the Vampyre (1979)** | **41.5** | **150** | **81%** | **0.67** |
| The Exorcist III | 44.6 | 108 | 64% | 0.24 |
| Apollo 18 | 56.3 | 223 | 53% | 0.20 |
| Sleepaway Camp | 65.3 | 131 | 39% | 0.18 |
| Day of the Dead | 56.5 | 150 | 54% | 0.13 |
| Little Shop of Horrors (1960) | 82.5 | 160 | 22% | 0.11 |
| Prom Night | 57.4 | 155 | 52% | 0.19 |
| Black Christmas | 30.6 | 95 | 97% | 0.27 |

Nosferatu matches on every axis, far beyond the runner-up:
- Identical darkness profile: <40 share 59% vs 59%, <60 share 81% vs 81%, max 148 vs 150.
- The signature bright slate-blue block at ~9–10% of runtime is the Carpathian mountain journey with pale blue-gray skies — target RGB (129,151,181) vs Nosferatu's (131,153,183), essentially identical.
- The scene-by-scene rhythm lines up: dark sepia mummy bookends at the start/end, candlelit inn browns at 13–18%, deep-blue night coach ride at ~21%, near-black castle interiors at 23–33%, gray plague-era Wismar streets mid-film, dark ending.

Every other candidate is ruled out on brightness (Sleepaway Camp, Little Shop, Apollo 18, Prom Night, Day of the Dead all far too bright), palette (Black Christmas is warm/red-brown, Little Shop is B&W-bright), or maximum luminance (Exorcist III never reaches the target's brightest block).

Answer: A
